items.title: Parse email statement messages entirely on device and emit structured events only
items.outcome: As a user, I can connect my mailbox and have statement and alert messages parsed on my own device, so a structured transaction event reaches the server while the message body never leaves the handset.
items.context: Raw email content never leaving the device is a hard rule, so email parsing cannot be a server capability. The connector, the parsers and the redaction all run on device, and the API only ever receives the same structured ingestion event that the message and notification sources already produce.
scope: On-device mailbox connector with least-privilege, revocable access and a narrow message filter
Deterministic on-device parsers for the supported issuer formats, with confidence and clarification routing
Structured ingestion event emission that carries amount, instant, issuer pattern identifier and confidence only
Extension of source precedence and deduplication so email events rank alongside message and notification events
Revocation that stops all fetching, clears cached message state on device and is verifiable
acceptance_criteria: No email body, subject, sender address or attachment is transmitted to the server or to any third party, proven by automated traffic capture on a release candidate
Parsing, redaction and confidence scoring all execute on device with the network disabled, proven by an instrumented test
Mailbox access uses the narrowest available scope and revoking it stops fetching immediately, proven by capture
A transaction arriving by both email and message deduplicates deterministically and the surviving record is explainable
A parser failure routes to on-device clarification rather than creating a wrong record or shipping the raw message for triage
Adding this source requires no change to the existing message and notification server paths
contracts_schema: Emits the published structured ingestion event; the email source is an additive registration and adds no free-text field
security_privacy: Raw email content is never persisted off device and never appears in logs, crash reports or support attachments
Connector credentials are held in the platform keystore and are revocable by the user at any time
Consent for mailbox access is a distinct purpose in the consent ledger and is revocable independently
observability: Publishes per-source ingestion counts, confidence distribution and deduplication outcomes
tests: Retention test proving no raw body persists
rollout_rollback: Behind a flag per source; email is enabled per cohort after the consent purpose is live
Rollback disables fetching and leaves already ingested records intact
non_goals: Server-side email fetching or parsing, permanently
Screen scraping or credential sharing with any bank, permanently
Aggregator connectivity, which is its own epic
Cash and ATM reconciliation, which T-ING-03 owns

items.title: Build on-device receipt capture and text recognition with user confirmation
items.outcome: As a user, I can photograph a paper receipt and have the amount, merchant and date extracted on my device, review what was read, and confirm before anything is recorded.
items.context: Receipts are the last common gap, particularly for cash. Doing the recognition on the device keeps the privacy promise intact, and requiring confirmation keeps a misread total from silently becoming a wrong balance.
scope: Camera capture with guidance for framing and lighting
On-device text recognition extracting amount, merchant, date and line items where present
Review screen showing what was extracted with every field editable
Confirmation required before any record is created
Image retention policy with a default that does not keep the photograph
Routing of low-confidence extractions to the existing clarification inbox
acceptance_criteria: Recognition runs entirely on the device and no image leaves it, verified by the traffic capture harness
No transaction is created without explicit user confirmation
Every extracted field is editable before confirmation
By default the photograph is not retained after confirmation, and retention is an explicit user choice
A low-confidence extraction routes to clarification rather than being applied
The capture and review screens are screen-reader traversable, with a manual entry path for users who cannot use the camera
contracts_schema: Submits a structured payload through the published ingestion contract; no image is ever submitted
security_privacy: Images are stored in application-private storage excluded from device backup and from media indexing
Camera permission is requested contextually and its purpose is recorded in the consent ledger
observability: Records capture attempts and confirmation outcomes without content
tests: Traffic capture test proving no image egress
rollout_rollback: Behind a flag, enabled per cohort after the capture evidence is attached
Rollback hides the capture entry point; confirmed transactions are unaffected
non_goals: Server-side image processing of any kind
Storing receipt images in the backend

items.title: Reconcile ATM withdrawals and cash spending against the existing manual entries
items.outcome: As a user who withdraws cash, I see the withdrawal as a movement into a cash account and I am prompted to reconcile it against the cash spending I already record by hand, so cash stops being a hole in the picture without asking me to re-enter what I already entered.
items.context: Manual cash entry already exists, so a second manual cash source would duplicate it. The gap is reconciliation: an ATM withdrawal is currently an expense rather than a transfer into cash held, and the manual cash entries are never matched against it.
scope: ATM withdrawal detection from existing ingested events, classified as a transfer into a cash account rather than as spending
Cash account balance derived from withdrawals in and manual cash entries out
Reconciliation prompt when the derived cash balance drifts beyond a stated threshold or a stated age
Adjustment entries recorded explicitly so a reconciliation never rewrites a prior entry
Precedence and deduplication rules so a withdrawal is not counted both as an expense and as a transfer
acceptance_criteria: An ATM withdrawal creates a transfer into the cash account and does not appear as spending in any report
The derived cash balance equals withdrawals in minus manual cash entries out plus adjustments, with no created or destroyed minor units
A reconciliation adjustment is a new explicit entry; no prior entry is mutated, proven by an append-only test
Users who never withdraw cash see no new prompt and no new account
A withdrawal ingested twice from two sources reconciles to one transfer, and the surviving record is explainable
All arithmetic agrees with the independent model, including the adjustment path
contracts_schema: Cash account and reconciliation adjustment expressed as additive registrations on the published ledger and ingestion contracts
security_privacy: Reconciliation prompts carry no counterparty text and no location data
Cash balances are ordinary ledger data and inherit the existing encryption and tenancy controls
observability: Reconciliation prompt shown, accepted and dismissed counts published without amounts
Drift distribution published so the threshold can be tuned without inspecting user data
tests: Property test asserting zero-sum across the withdrawal, the manual entry and the adjustment
Deduplication test for a withdrawal observed on two sources
Regression test proving existing manual cash entry behaviour is unchanged
rollout_rollback: Shipped behind a flag defaulting to off; enabled for users who have at least one detected withdrawal
Rollback disables detection and prompts; already-created transfers remain valid ledger entries
non_goals: A second manual cash entry surface, which already exists
Cash forecasting, which belongs to the income and budgeting epic
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo api. Owns detection, the cash account derivation and the adjustment entry. Client surfaces reuse the existing clarification and transaction contracts.
